## Validation and scope

The strategy retrieved **all 14 unique screened relevant records** in the known-record sets: 100% relative recall for the development sets and for the three-record held-out validation set. The validation set was split from the pilot sample and repeatedly checked during evaluation, so it is **semi-independent**, not fully independent; this recall does not establish absolute sensitivity.

The outcomes block was tested and left out: it reduced retrieval by 25.9%, and none of its 30 sampled excluded records met the eligibility criteria. Comparator and controlled design were left for screening. I treated clinically oriented computer cases, screen-based simulations, and videodisc patient scenarios as potentially eligible virtual environments even when authors did not call them “VR.” That broad interpretation supports sensitivity but may add records for screening.

The protected report passed, and the internal critique closed its findings. **PRESS peer review by an information specialist is still needed before use.**
